newsitem.title: MEXICO: Powerful Mexican union boss sick in hospital.
newsitem.headline: Powerful Mexican union boss sick in hospital.

text.p: Veteran union boss Fidel Velazquez, who has swung Mexican workers behind the government for more than half a century, is ill and has been admitted to a hospital, a hospital official said on Wednesday.
The official, who declined to give her name, told reporters that Velazquez was admitted to Mexico City's smart ABC Hospital on Tuesday. The hospital initially denied that Velazquez was inside.
Velazquez, 96, is the president of the Confederation of Mexican Workers (CTM), which claims to represent seven million workers and has been a bedrock of government support for decades.
His illness came at a delicate time for the government as it prepares for annual negotiations with workers and employers on a new economic programme for 1997.

Velazquez's ageing nephew Luis Velazquez earlier dismissed reports that his uncle was sick, telling reporters that he had gone to the hospital for a routine checkup earlier in the day. "He is standing and in very good humour," Velazquez said.
Salomon Jasqui, Velazquez's doctor, was due to give a news conference later in the day.

Fidel's relatives have given misleading information in the past about his health during illnesses or delicate operations, partly to avoid speculation about a resignation that could lead to a fiercely contested succession at the CTM.
